findings.evidence: Lines 196–214 use `hμ` only to establish `μ ∈ interlacingShapes n μ`. `YoungDiagram.mem_interlacingShapes` at lines 201 and 210 ensures every indexed `ν` has at most `n` rows and lies inside `μ`; when `μ` has more than `n` rows, such a `ν` cannot equal `μ`, hence `ν.card < μ.card` and its zero power vanishes.
findings.fix: Remove `hμ` and prove the existing case when `μ.colLen 0 ≤ n`; in the complementary case, use the branching formula to kill every summand and `diagramSchurPoly_eq_zero_of_lt_colLen` for the right-hand side.
findings.issue: `aeval_snoc_zero_diagramSchurPoly` unnecessarily assumes `μ.colLen 0 ≤ n`. If the bound fails, every `ν ∈ interlacingShapes n μ` is still strictly smaller than `μ`, so every summand in the branching formula contains a positive power of the specialized zero variable, while `diagramSchurPoly n R μ = 0`.

summary: The stability theorem is stated with an unnecessary row-bound assumption; the zero-specialization identity naturally holds for every Young diagram.
